bull.b: Demand is growing across several ophthalmic franchises rather than relying on a single product. VEVYE is gaining prescriptions and share, while IHEEZO and TRIESENCE are setting unit records, supporting a broader and potentially more durable revenue base.

bull.t: Strong cash generation and product economics
bull.b: The shift to positive operating and free cash flow improves near-term liquidity and demonstrates better cash conversion than reported earnings alone suggest. Combined with high gross margins, this gives Harrow resources to support commercialization while working toward more consistent profitability.

TYRVAYA expands Harrow’s dry-eye offering beyond eye drops and can give physicians another treatment option based on patient tolerance and mechanism. The broader portfolio may improve salesforce productivity, deepen category positioning, and create an additional growth platform after integration.

bear.t: Elevated leverage and thin equity cushion
bear.b: A debt-funded balance sheet reduces financial flexibility if operating results weaken or integration requires more capital. The thin equity cushion increases exposure to refinancing pressure and potential dilution, making sustained cash generation and disciplined capital allocation especially important.

High gross margins have not yet translated into durable earnings because operating costs or other headwinds remain substantial. Continued losses can constrain reinvestment, weaken balance-sheet resilience, and make the company more dependent on successful revenue growth and expense control.

bear.t: Execution risk from required second-half ramp
bear.b: Meeting guidance requires a much faster revenue pace in the second half than achieved in the first half. That acceleration depends on channel normalization, continued VEVYE growth, salesforce productivity, and TYRVAYA closing and integration, creating meaningful execution risk over coming quarters.
